messages:
ravi: WIP: sketching a 'migration bridges' approach for model catalog lifecycle. Goal: reduce customer churn during forced moves and make deprecations predictable. Thoughts on lanes, incentives, and technical hooks.
emma: love the name. what are migration bridges? quick tl;dr?
ravi: short: small runtime compatibility adapters + tenant grace tokens + rolling canaries. three bridge types: instant (fast opt-in), negotiated (3090d with credits), and legacy bridge (6mo grace, full shim).
carlos: for negotiated lane, recommend offering 3 free migration credits per fiscal quarter to large customers. sales can trade extra credits.
jordan: technical: bridge needs two things: 1) runtime adapter to remap request params/tokenizer/response fields, 2) telemetry tag so we can split metrics by bridge usage. both are doable.
ops-bot: Reminder: model artifact retention policy currently 90 days. Change requests must be filed in infra backlog.
cs_olivia: customers ask for 'no surprise' deprecations. they want: explicit calendar, sample prompts to validate, and a fail-safe rollback toggle.
emma: acceptance criteria proposal: quality drop < 2% absolute on primary metric (task-specific), hallucination delta < 0.5pp, p95 latency increase < 30%. if any breach, hold rollout.
ravi: agree. also propose tokenized sample sets: onboarding (n=250), staged (n=1,000), release (n=5,000). smaller than some proposals but easier to run across many models.
carlos: note on pinning: introduce 'pin TTL' (default 90d for free tenants, 180d for enterprise). pin API should allow tenant-admin to renew or release.
jordan: implementation cost: pin TTL requires storage + metadata; renewing should be a single API call that checkpoints the model fingerprint. cheap.
ops-bot: FYI: quantized backup artifacts ~80GB per 13B model. retention of extra versions will increase S3 costs.
cs_olivia: CS asks that we create a one-click 'test migration' in Console that runs a representative prompt set and surfaces diffs. customers can then accept or request rollback.
emma: rollout gate cadence: 0.5% of traffic -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. each step min 24h and metric gate checks. allow manual pause.
ravi: deprecation cadence proposal: announcement window = 60d for negotiated, 120d for legacy. auto-migrate only for soft-pin tenants; hard-pinned tenants require opt-in or contract amendment.
carlos: contract/legal will need specific language for hard-pin obligations. add to legal intake.
jordan: shim adapter design note: keep it isolated as a sidecar so we can version adapters independently of serving runtime. helps rollback.
emma: bench harness command for reproducibility (dev-only):
```
bench-run --model=modelY:v4 --input=bench_queries.json --iters=3000 --seq=256 --metrics=bleu,f1,latency_p95
```
capture both quality and token-based cost.
cs_olivia: comms plan: pre-announce -> validation window with test harness -> migration week -> final cut. include copy for customer-facing emails and in-app banners.
ravi: decision points for RFC: 1) migration bridge types + timelines 2) pin TTL defaults 3) bench sample sizes 4) rollout cadence 5) comm windows + credits.
emma: I'm comfortable with the metrics and cadence. prefer slightly larger release sample (5k vs 10k later) but okay as written.
carlos: i'll draft the migration credit policy and legal blurb.
jordan: i'll spike the sidecar shim and drop a PR with adapter spec.
cs_olivia: CS will draft test-harness UI copy and sample-prompt packs for top 20 customers.
ravi: thanks team 1: i'll open RFC and tickets for infra + console + legal. target: RFC ready by Wed.
emma: ack.
carlos: ack.
jordan: ack.
ops-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-3124 (model retention extension request).
ravi: adding @sales for awareness on credits/offers.
cs_olivia: also flag @support; they need playbooks if customers hit regressions.
